items.question: Which studies in the evidence tested flames on aircraft in partial gravity?
items.answer:
From the evidence ledger (values as reported, no conversion):
- FM2 poster: lunar-gravity centrifuge and parabolic flight; SIBAL fabric (cotton/fiberglass blend); lunar (simulated); air: burning behaviour = burns (only downward) [R076]
- LUCI: Blue Origin New Shepard NS-29, spinning capsule; PMMA (acrylic) rod; lunar (simulated by capsule spin); normal pressure; air: flame tip spread rate = 0.15 cm/s [R007]
- LUCI: Blue Origin New Shepard NS-29, spinning capsule; SIBAL fabric (cotton-fiberglass); lunar (simulated by capsule spin); normal pressure; air: flame width during semi-steady spread = 3.2 cm (approximate) [R019]
- Feier et al.: NASA KC-135 aircraft; thin cellulose (Kimwipes); 0.10, 0.16 and 0.38 G; 0.2-0.4 atm; 21% O2, balance N2: time within 15% of nominal acceleration = 5-20 s (range) [R097]
- Feier et al.: NASA KC-135 aircraft; thin cellulose (Kimwipes); 0.1, 0.16 and 0.38 G; 0.2-0.4 atm; 21% O2, balance N2: partial-gravity parabolas per flight = 10 (upper bound) [R098]
- Sacksteder et al.: NASA KC-135 aircraft; Kimwipes thin cellulosic tissue; partial gravity (0.1, 0.16, 0.38 g); 27.6 kPa (4.0 psia); air: gravity level at which downward spread rate peaks = 0.38 g (approximate) [R093]
- Sacksteder et al.: NASA KC-135 aircraft; Kimwipes thin cellulosic tissue; partial gravity (0.1, 0.16, 0.38 g); 27.6 kPa; air: dependence of upward spread rate on gravity = linear [R092]
